708653.t: From Proto-Hellenic *mégas, from a conflation of Proto-Indo-European *méǵh₂s (“great”) with its derivative *meǵh₂los (“great”).

708695.t: From Proto-Hellenic *mélans, from a derivation of Proto-Indo-European *melh₂- (“dark, black”). The feminine -αινα (-aina) originates from *-ih₂ via metathesis; see -ια (-ia).

708610.t: Traditionally derived from a Proto-Indo-European *maǵʰ- (“to fight”), though Beekes considers Pre-Greek origin more likely. See also Old Armenian մաքառիմ (makʻaṙim, “to combat, quarrel”), which may continue the same root.

708682.t: Alteration of older μέζων (mézōn), perhaps after ἀμείνων (ămeínōn), from Proto-Hellenic *méd͏̌d͏̌ōn, from Proto-Indo-European *méǵyōs, from *méǵh₂s (“great”), whence μέγας (mégăs). Synchronically, μέγας (mégăs) + *-ϳων (*-jōn).

708699.t: According to Beekes, a back-formation from μελετάω (meletáō). Connected with μέλω (mélō).

708690.t: Explained by the ancients as deriving from μέλας (mélas, “black”), because of the soot which accumulates on the ceiling.

708697.t: As for its accent, this word agrees with secondary adjectives like χρύσεος (khrúseos), λίθεος (lítheos), βόεος (bóeos), but conceptually it rather belongs to primary oxytones, like ἐτεός (eteós), κενεός (keneós), στερεός (stereós).

708687.t: According to Beekes, from a noun, perhaps *μεῖρος (*meîros), which would agree with Sanskrit मर्य॑ (márya, “young man; suitor; lover”) and Avestan 𐬨𐬀𐬌𐬭𐬌𐬌𐬀 (maⁱriia, “yeoman”), or *μεῖρα (*meîră).

708680.t: From Proto-Indo-European *smey-. Cognates include Latin miror, comis, Sanskrit स्मयते (smáyate), Old Norse *smīla (English smile).
